items.title: MARC upgrades SAJ Capital sukuk, outlook stable
items.summary: SAJ Capital is a wholly-owned funding vehicle of Ranhill Capital Sdn Bhd, which owns an 80 per cent stake in Ranhill SAJ, Johor's sole source-to-tap water services provider. Given its reliance on dividends from Ranhill SAJ to meet its sukuk obligations, SAJ Capital's rating is driven by Ranhill SAJ's credit strength. MARC said the upgrade reflects Ranhill SAJ's materially stronger credit profile, underpinned by sustained improvements in operating performance, cash flow generation and financial flexibility.

items.title: MACC remands three more over alleged RM450,000 misuse of penalty payments
items.summary: Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah issued the remand order until Aug 9 against the three men, who are in their 50s, following an application by the MACC at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court today. According to a MACC source, the three were arrested at the commission’s headquarters at about 6 pm yesterday. Meanwhile, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests and said the case was being investigated under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Malaysian arrested in Singapore with 9kg cannabis, 530g meth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 22-year-old Malaysian man has been arrested in Singapore for attempting to smuggle drugs worth about RM1.15 million into the republic. The case follows recent arrests of Malaysians abroad, including a pilot and another man in Indonesia, for similar drug trafficking activities. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police had received information on the arrest and had launched follow-up investigations to identify those behind the cross-border syndicate.

items.title: UK PM Burnham considering inquiry into Epstein, minister says
items.summary: LONDON: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is looking at holding a public inquiry into the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and his actions in the UK, victims minister Alex Davies-Jones told the BBC. In a report released on Tuesday, Wyden alleged that Bank of America, Deutsche Bank and JPMorgan Chase may have violated federal anti-money laundering laws by failing to report Epstein's suspicious transactions in a timely manner. Bank of America failed to properly screen and report US$170 million in payments to Epstein, Wyden's report said, adding that the bank years later concluded in suspicious activity reports that the transactions had no verifiable business purpose.

items.title: Shafee seeks to strike out parts of Tony Pua's statement in 1MDB suit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah has applied to expunge large portions of former DAP lawmaker Tony Pua's witness statement in the US$5.64 billion 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) civil suit against Datuk Seri Najib Razak and several others. At the outset of today's hearing, Shafee said the former Damansara MP's statement was largely based on hearsay and personal opinion. Shafee said Pua should not substitute his personal account for official records, particularly where the matters could be established through the PAC report or parliamentary proceedings.

items.title: Girl's viral video in car with missing rear windshield brings help to family
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A viral video showing a young girl waving at motorists from a car without a rear windshield has led social activist Adrian Edy to a family struggling with financial hardship. The encounter with the family of seven taught the 30-year-old a valuable lesson about finding happiness despite living a modest life, after the father whom he called 'Pakcik Ambarat' told him he remained grateful for his old second-hand Proton Iswara despite being unable to work. The car was missing its rear windshield.

items.title: GOF records 813 arrests involving various enforcement operations in 4 states
items.summary: Its commander, SAC Balveer Singh Mahindar Singh, said that in the same period the total number of cases also increased to 389 cases compared to 291 cases recorded during the same period last year, which is an increase of 98 cases or 33.68 per cent. For roadblock operations conducted in seven locations in northern Peninsular Malaysia, Balveer Singh said that 75 cases were recorded this year compared to 24 cases during the same period last year. He said the operations also recorded 89 arrests, an increase from 30 arrests last year, or a 196 per cent increase.

items.title: Prison officer arrested over RM3,000 bribe to smuggle contraband into jail
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A prison officer has been arrested over allegations of soliciting and accepting about RM3,000 in bribes to smuggle prohibited items into a prison. A Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) source said the suspect was arrested at about 11.50am yesterday at his home in Sungai Petani, Kedah. Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect, in his 20s, allegedly committed the offence in March while serving at a prison in Melaka.

items.title: High Court acquits temple chairman over alleged trespass at Sri Maha Mariamman temple
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — The High Court today acquitted a temple chairman who had been charged with trespassing at the Sri Maha Mariamman Temple on privately owned land last year, Sinar Harian reported. Lawyer Latheefa Koya, who represented M Paramaguru, 49, said Justice Hazlina Hussain quashed the charge after finding it was fatally defective. In a statement, Latheefa said the court ruled the charge failed to disclose the criminal intent required to constitute the offence of trespass.

items.title: RM10.68m drug-laced vape syndicate busted in Johor, seven arrested
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police crippled a syndicate processing and distributing drug-infused vape cartridges worth RM10.68 million following the arrest of seven suspects, in five simultaneous raids across the state on Sunday. Johor deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Hoo Chuan Huat said the suspects, aged between 36 and 46, comprised six men, including a foreign man and a foreign woman. Hoo said following that raid, police seized 47 plastic bottles containing vape flavours, a glass bottle containing 127.55 litres of liquid methamphetamine worth RM6.37 million, two packets of cocaine weighing 410g, a packet of ketamine weighing 40g, as well as machines and equipment used to fill the vape cartridges.

items.title: Bersatu tells Azeez to clarify if MACC contacted him over TH RCI findings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu has called on former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim to clarify whether he has been summoned or contacted by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) over findings from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the institution. The party's supreme council member Dr Afif Bahardin said Azeez, who had claimed to have a 2021 letter from the MACC chief commissioner clearing him of any involvement, must make the document public. Afif also called on the MACC and the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) to carry out investigations and make any prosecution decisions independently, professionally and without bias.

items.title: Selangor AI White Paper to outline landscape, map benefits, challenges, value proposition, says MB
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — The Selangor government’s artificial intelligence (AI) White Paper, which is currently being developed, will outline the overall landscape for the use of the technology, including its challenges, benefits and value proposition. “The AI White Paper will serve as a guideline for us, particularly in Selangor, on how we should approach, live with and interact with AI,” he said. Amirudin said the AI White Paper would be tabled at the State Legislative Assembly for debate at a later date.

items.title: High Court acquits temple chairman, quashes trespass charge
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A temple chairman was acquitted by the High Court today after it quashed a criminal trespass charge against him, ruling that it failed to disclose the necessary element of intent. Lawyer Latheefa Koya, in a statement, said judge Dr Hazlina Hussain found that the charge against M. Paramaguru, 49, did not state that he had the intention to commit an offence, a key ingredient of criminal trespass. The alleged offence was said to have taken place at 4.45pm on June 19 last year.

items.title: Kulasegaran: Security laws must not erode human rights
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Efforts to strengthen national security must not come at the expense of human rights, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department for Law and Institutional Reform M. Kulasegaran said. "Legal reform had become increasingly important as technology, society and security threats continued to evolve. "No single institution can confront national security threats alone.

items.title: Sabah police need to leverage technology, says state police chief
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah police must leverage technological advancements to improve work efficiency, particularly in investigations and the preparation of investigation papers, said state police commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun. He said that early in his career, most tasks, including preparing investigation papers, were carried out manually and took longer to complete. The ceremony saw Superintendent Syed Lot Syed Abdul Rahman hand over duties as Kota Kinabalu district police chief to Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain..

items.title: India monsoon floods, landslides kill more than 100 since July
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Floods and landslides triggered by monsoon rains have killed more than 100 people across India since July, official data showed Wednesday, with thousands forced to flee their inundated homes. India's northeastern state of Assam is among the hardest hit by the annual rains, with at least 87 people killed, according to Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma. In the state's worst-affected Sivasagar district, some 47 people have been killed as several areas remain under water.

items.title: Tech stocks dominate Bursa again amid fresh optimism
items.summary: The rally extended gains from last Friday, when Bursa Malaysia's technology sector tracked a powerful overnight surge in Wall Street technology stocks led by Microsoft. By the midday break, the Bursa Malaysia Technology Index had climbed 2.91 per cent to 77.83, its highest level since July 18, 2024. Technology and technology-linked counters dominated the exchange's most active list, led by NationGate Holdings Bhd, Inari Amertron Bhd, Zetrix AI Bhd, VS Industry Bhd and SNS Network Technology Bhd.

items.title: US cooling giant picks Nilai for US$150mil plant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: US-based sustainable cooling solutions provider BAC will invest US$150 million to establish a new manufacturing facility in Nilai, Negri Sembilan. Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) said the investment is expected to create up to 200 high-skilled jobs by 2035, including high-skilled engineering and professional roles. The project was marked by a groundbreaking ceremony today, attended by Mida deputy chief executive officer (Investment Development) Zuaida Abdullah, BAC president Don Fetzer and BAC global vice president and Asia Pacific head Ted Lim.

items.title: MCMC, chairman reach out-of-court defamation settlement with Chegubard
items.summary: The defamation suit was filed by the MCMC and its chairman at the Seremban High Court on May 14, 2025, over a post made by Badrul on his Facebook account. Lawyer Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, who represented Badrul, said the parties agreed to seek a resolution through a mediation session conducted today. Alhamdulillah, today, both parties agreed," he said when met at the Seremban Court Complex.

items.title: Nine more open spaces gazetted to strengthen KL's green space protection
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is stepping up efforts to safeguard Kuala Lumpur's green spaces with the gazettement of nine additional open areas, aimed at ensuring city development remains balanced while preserving public recreational areas. The nine newly gazetted open spaces include Lot 82448 in the Batu sub-district, near Desa ParkCity Lake (6,607sqm or 1.632 acres); Lot 82443 in the Batu sub-district, also near Desa ParkCity Lake (22,000sqm or 5.436 acres); Lot 202030 in the Setapak sub-district, near Bayu Sentul Condominium (13,882 square metres or 3.430 acres); and Lot 38500 in the Petaling sub-district, near Residensi Jalil Mas (529 square metres or 0.130 acres). Other newly gazetted open spaces include Lot 25119 in the Setapak sub-district, near Masjid Salahuddin Al-Ayubbi in Taman Melati (1,456sqm or 0.359 acres); Lot 39399 in the Petaling sub-district, near East Bukit Jalil Condominium (1,658 square metres or 0.409 acres); Lot 39397 in the Petaling sub-district, also near East Bukit Jalil Condominium (185 sqm or 0.045 acres); Lot 56219 in the Batu sub-district, near United Point Mall (3,679sqm); and Lot 482950 in the Kuala Lumpur suib-district, near Padang TURF Tasik Permaisuri (1,505 sqm or 0.371 acres).

items.title: Body found in a net: Two more men arrested
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police have arrested two more men over the murder of a man whose body was found bound and wrapped in a net in Sungai Tanjung, Parit Raja, on Sunday. Johor deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Hoo Chuan Huat said the suspects, aged 33 and 34, were picked up in Kluang and Johor Baru yesterday. "The three suspects arrested earlier have been remanded for seven days until Aug 10, while the two suspects arrested yesterday have also been remanded until the same date," he told a press conference.

items.title: Asian stocks hit multi-week highs as easing US-Iran tensions lift risk appetite
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Most emerging Asian equities climbed to multi-week highs and regional currencies strengthened on Wednesday as hopes of easing US-Iran tensions boosted risk appetite and kept oil prices below US$80 a barrel. The MSCI emerging markets Asia equities index rose about three per cent to a two-week high, while the EM currencies gauge gained 0.4 per cent to an all-time high. Taiwan's tech-heavy benchmark followed suit, jumping 3.4 per cent.

items.title: 'Like the end of the world': Eclipse chasers flocking to Spain
items.summary: It is this awe-inspiring experience that will draw people from all over the world to northern Spain next week in the hope of witnessing a total solar eclipse. "It's very sad," Warning said. "A total eclipse is not something you see, it's something you experience," he told AFP.

items.title: Pakistani man charged with molesting woman in parked car in Batu Pahat
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A Pakistani perfume salesman was charged in the magistrate's court today with outraging the modesty of a woman he had recently met, inside a vehicle earlier this month. Umair Iqbal Sheikh, 33, a father of three, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno. He is accused of using criminal force with intent to outrage the modesty of a 26-year-old woman inside a parked car at Taman Sri Jaya at 4.30pm on Aug 1.

items.title: Cops investigate housebreaking, robbery in Tanjung Bungah; CCTV shows lone suspect in five‑day crime spree
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 5 — Police have opened investigation papers into four crimes reported in Tanjung Bungah between July 28 and August 2, involving housebreaking, robbery, trespassing and theft. Northeast district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said two of the four cases resulted in losses estimated at about RM17,000, while the other two caused no losses, refuting claims circulating on social media that five incidents had occurred in the area. He said police believed a man wearing a red shirt seen in CCTV footage could be linked to some of the incidents, although investigations were ongoing to establish the connection.

items.title: China's yuan hits its strongest in 3-1/2 years as trade tensions grow
items.summary: SHANGHAI: China's yuan hit its strongest level in 3-1/2 years on Wednesday, as escalating trade and geopolitical tensions add to pressure for the currency to appreciate. The Chinese currency was also bolstered by a softer dollar index, as easing Middle East tensions weakened the greenback's appeal. The US dollar index slipped about 0.1 per cent.

items.title: Selangor AI White Paper to outline landscape, address challenges - Amirudin
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government's artificial intelligence (AI) White Paper, which is currently being developed, will outline the overall landscape for the use of the technology, including its challenges, benefits and value proposition. "The AI White Paper will serve as a guideline for us, particularly in Selangor, on how we should approach, live with and interact with AI," he said. Amirudin said the AI White Paper would be tabled at the State Legislative Assembly for debate at a later date.

items.title: College student held over newborn's death remanded for another day
items.summary: The Magistrate's Court granted the police extension to facilitate investigations under Section 302 and Section 315 of the Penal Code for murder and causing death after birth. Kluang police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said the extension would allow police to complete their probe. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad previously said police received a report that a female student had been admitted to Enche' Besar Hajjah Kalsom Hospital after giving birth.

items.title: Selangor fine‑tunes new model for WiFi Smart Selangor reimplementation, says state exco
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — The Selangor government, through Smartsel Sdn Bhd, is fine-tuning a new model for the reimplementation of the WiFi Smart Selangor (WSS) initiative, taking into account various factors, including changing user needs. State Islamic Affairs and Innovation Committee chairman Mohd Fahmi Ngah said the new free WiFi model would also take into consideration usage levels at each location, infrastructure capacity, as well as a more sustainable funding and operational mechanism. Mohd Fahmi said the new model was developed after the state government decided to adopt a more sustainable and resilient service delivery model.

items.title: Hire more judges, boost training to cut court backlog, says former CJ
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Increasing the number of judges and ensuring continuous training are key to reducing the court backlog and strengthening judicial expertise in an increasingly complex world, former chief justice Tun Zaki Azmi said. He said reforms introduced by Chief Justice Tun Wan Farid Wan Salleh reflect many of the measures implemented during his own tenure. "Judges must keep learning because no judge knows everything," he said at the 2nd Wisdom Malaysia 2026 Conference today.

items.title: GOF seizes RM9.39m worth of illegal e‑waste in Ipoh raids, 14 arrested
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 5 — The General Operations Force (GOF) Northern Brigade seized 120,220 kilogrammes of electronic waste (e-waste) worth about RM9.39 million, along with processing machinery, during raids on three premises around Ipoh on Aug 3. Its commander SAC Balveer Singh Mahindar Singh said the operation also led to the arrest of 14 individuals aged between 20 and 50, comprising two local men believed to be the premises managers and 12 Myanmar workers, including eight men and four women. He said intelligence gathered over a week found that the three premises were allegedly processing e-waste without approval from the Department of Environment (DOE), while operating under the guise of recycling factories.

items.title: Gamuda lands RM1.7bil hyperscale data centre job in Negri Sembilan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd has secured a RM1.71 billion contract from a United States-headquartered multinational technology company to build a hyperscale data centre in Port Dickson, Negri Sembilan. The construction job was awarded to its subsidiary Gamuda Engineering Sdn Bhd, according to the company's bourse filing. The project, which is on a build-only contract basis, involves constructing a single-storey hyperscale data centre facility comprising site infrastructure works, building core and shell construction, as well as mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) fit-out works.

items.title: Court to decide if Rosmah can defer RM67.5mil payment to Lebanese jeweller
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has fixed Aug 12 to decide whether Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor can defer payment of RM67.5 million to Lebanese jewellery company Global Royalty Trading SAL. Rosmah was represented by lawyer Mohd Reza Rahim, while Global Royalty was represented by lawyer Venothani Rajagopal. On June 10, High Court judge Datuk Quay Chew Soon ordered Rosmah, 75, to pay RM67.5 million to Global Royalty over 43 pieces of jewellery allegedly loaned to her.

items.title: [UPDATED] Three more arrested in MACC's Tabung Haji RCI probe over RM450,000 penalty notices
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested three more people in connection with its investigation into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) over alleged misappropriation involving about RM450,000 in Notice of Penalty (NOP) charges. An MACC source said the three were arrested at about 6pm yesterday after they turned up at the commission's headquarters to assist investigations. On July 31, MACC launched its probe into the RCI report by sending an eight-member team to TH's headquarters to identify relevant documents and materials.

items.title: Ops Sapu: 81 undocumented migrants held at Kedah construction site
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 5 — The Kedah Immigration Department arrested 81 undocumented migrants during Ops Sapu at a construction site in Kuala Kedah yesterday. The department said the operation, which began at 9.50am, was carried out following intelligence gathering and public tip-offs, and involved 19 officers from its Immigration Action Unit under the Enforcement Division. “A total of 81 undocumented migrants were arrested, comprising 73 men and eight women, namely 42 Bangladeshis, 26 Indonesians, 10 Myanmar nationals, one Pakistani and two Indians,” the department said in a statement.

items.title: Poachers exploit northern border, Malayan tigers remain top target list
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's northern land border has become the main entry point for foreign poachers, particularly from Vietnam, seeking to hunt endangered wildlife, including the critically endangered Malayan tiger. Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said syndicates use illegal border crossings to enter the country before moving into forest reserves believed to be home to their target species. Zaki said other targeted species include elephants, pangolins, deer, hornbills, exotic birds, reptiles and protected primates.

items.title: PLUS opens tenders for next phase of Juru-Sungai Dua traffic dispersal project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — PLUS Malaysia Bhd (PLUS) has opened tenders for Packages 2 and 5 of the Juru-Sungai Dua Traffic Dispersal Project (PTJSD) as the project enters its next phase, with Package 1 recording an overall physical progress of 34.63 per cent as of July 31. In a statement today, PLUS said the tender process for Packages 2 and 5 was underway, marking another milestone in the implementation of the project. Under Package 1, utility relocation works have reached 75 per cent completion, while geotechnical works along Jalan Tun Hussein Onn, including the construction of a new bridge, have achieved 68 per cent completion.

items.title: GOF seizes RM9.39mil worth of illegal e-waste in Ipoh raids
items.summary: IPOH: The General Operations Force (GOF) Northern Brigade seized 120,220kg of electronic waste (e-waste) worth about RM9.39 million, along with processing machinery, during raids on three premises around Ipoh on Aug 3. Its commander SAC Balveer Singh Mahindar Singh said the operation also led to the arrest of 14 people aged between 20 and 50, comprising two local men believed to be the premises managers and 12 Myanmar workers, including eight men and four women. He said intelligence gathered over a week found that the three premises were allegedly processing e-waste without approval from the Department of Environment (DOE), while operating under the guise of recycling factories.

items.title: SPM 2025 holders can now apply for Public Service Dept’s Dermasiswa B40 scholarships until Aug 16
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — The Public Service Department (PSD) has opened applications for the 2026 Dermasiswa B40 (DB40) programme for 2025 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) holders from eligible B40 families to pursue diploma studies at institutions of higher learning in the country. PSD said applications for the programme are open from 2pm on August 3, 2026 (Monday), until 5pm on August 16, 2026 (Sunday), via the PSD Sponsorship Portal at https://penajaan.jpa.gov.my . “Through the programme, students have the opportunity to pursue diploma studies at selected public universities, polytechnics, MARA TVET institutions and Public Skills Training Institutes (ILKA) in strategic fields that support the country’s human capital development,” PSD said in a statement.

items.title: Teen’s remand extended over death of newborn found with stab wounds in Kluang
items.summary: KLUANG, Aug 5 — A 19-year-old college student’s remand has been extended by one day to assist investigations into the death of a newborn baby found with stab wounds in a house toilet here late last month. The remand extension order was issued by Magistrate Nurasidah A. Rahman at the Magistrate’s Court here today. Further investigations at the rented house where the female student lived in Taman Setia Mutiara led to the discovery of a deceased female baby in the toilet.

items.title: Driver and wife injured after MPV hits herd of wild elephants on LPT2 near Chukai
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 5 — A couple were injured after their multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) collided with a herd of wild elephants at Kilometre 274.6 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2), after the Cheneh Toll Plaza, near here last night. Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said the 10.20pm incident left Abdul Wahid Ismail, 55, with minor injuries to his left hand, while his wife, Fauziah Muda, 52, injured her right hand. “Initial investigations found that Abdul Wahid was driving a Toyota Estima MPV in the left lane when he came upon a herd of wild elephants on the road.

items.title: Car crashes into Klang pastry shop after driver selects wrong gear, injuring assistant
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — A shop assistant was injured after a car crashed into a pastry shop in Taman Berkeley, Klang, at about 3.30pm yesterday. North Klang District Police chief ACP Ramsay Embol said the crash was believed to have occurred when a woman in her early 50s selected the wrong gear and accidentally pressed the accelerator while leaving a parking space outside the shop after making a purchase. “The shop assistant, a woman in her early 30s, was rushed to KPJ Klang Hospital for treatment, while the car driver, who was also injured, was taken to Sunway Medical Centre,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Rosmah seeks stay on RM67.4m ruling, cites RM100,000 bank balance and concerns over jeweller’s finances
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Counsel for Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor today sought a stay of execution on a court order requiring her to pay RM67.4 million to Lebanese jeweller Global Royalty Trading SAL, saying she has only about RM100,000 in her bank account and there is “simply no mechanism” to verify the Beirut-based firm’s financial standing. Rosmah’s lawyer Reza Rahim said the plaintiff’s affidavit failed to provide any details of its bank accounts, available funds or other assets, leaving no evidence that it could guarantee repayment of the RM67.4 million if Rosmah succeeded on appeal. Today was the High Court’s hearing of Rosmah’s application to stay the High Court’s decision from June 10 this year.

items.title: Man found dead at Tanjung Rambutan care facility, police launch murder probe
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 5 — Police have launched an investigation into the death of a 54-year-old local man at a nursing home in Tanjung Rambutan yesterday. In a statement today, Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said Tanjung Rambutan Police Station was informed by the Tanjung Rambutan Health Clinic about the death of a resident at the care facility at 2pm. He said initial police checks at the scene revealed several injuries on the victim’s body.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh announces nine more KL open spaces gazetted to protect green areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The government is stepping up efforts to safeguard Kuala Lumpur’s green spaces with the gazettement of nine additional open areas, aimed at ensuring city development remains balanced while preserving public recreational areas. The nine newly gazetted open spaces include Lot 82448 in the Batu sub-district, near Desa ParkCity Lake (6,607 square metres or 1.632 acres); Lot 82443 in the Batu sub-district, also near Desa ParkCity Lake (22,000 square metres or 5.436 acres); Lot 202030 in the Setapak sub-district, near Bayu Sentul Condominium (13,882 square metres or 3.430 acres); and Lot 38500 in the Petaling sub-district, near Residensi Jalil Mas (529 square metres or 0.130 acres). Other newly gazetted open spaces include Lot 25119 in the Setapak sub-district, near Masjid Salahuddin Al-Ayubbi in Taman Melati (1,456 square metres or 0.359 acres); Lot 39399 in the Petaling sub-district, near East Bukit Jalil Condominium (1,658 square metres or 0.409 acres); Lot 39397 in the Petaling sub-district, also near East Bukit Jalil Condominium (185 square metres or 0.045 acres); Lot 56219 in the Batu sub-district, near United Point Mall (3,679 square metres); and Lot 482950 in the Kuala Lumpur suib-district, near Padang TURF Tasik Permaisuri (1,505 square metres or 0.371 acres).

items.title: Court orders former senator to pay Salim Fateh Din RM275,000 over two disputes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Former senator Datuk Daljit Singh has reportedly been ordered to pay Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) executive vice-chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din a total of RM275,000 following judgments in two separate cases. Free Malaysia Today reported that High Court judge Roz Mawar Rozain awarded Mohamad Salim RM100,000 in defamation damages and RM75,000 in costs, and issued an injunction on July 30 barring Daljit from repeating the defamatory statements. Mohamad Salim filed the suit in June 2023 over the words “Salim cheated me”, which Daljit allegedly said in Malay to lawyer Selva Kumar Mookiah in 2021, before sending him a text message about Mohamad Salim the following morning.

items.title: Sanusi issues LODs to Nga Kor Ming, two others over alleged distortion of remarks
items.summary: ALOR STAR, Aug 5 — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has issued letters of demand (LOD) to DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming and two others accused of distorting his remarks at a recent ceramah in Negri Sembilan, the New Straits Times reported. The report said Sanusi had also issued an LOD to Salim Abd Rahman, while former Skudai assemblyman Marina Ibrahim was scheduled to receive hers. Sanusi said those who distorted facts, embellished or twisted his statements would also receive LODs.

items.title: Customs dept busts smuggling operations involving alcohol, assorted goods worth RM12.2m
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 5 — The Royal Malaysian Customs Department has uncovered smuggling activities involving assorted goods and alcoholic beverages in two separate raids in early July, with the total seizure value exceeding RM12.2 million, including taxes. Negeri Sembilan Customs director Jamal Paiman said the seized items from both cases were valued at an estimated RM4.67 million, while the taxes involved amounted to RM7.60 million. “The seized assorted goods and the lorry were valued at approximately RM640,268, with unpaid duties and taxes estimated at RM69,873.48.

items.title: MACC arrests former CEO, CFO over alleged abuse of power in RM370m plantation deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested the former chief executive officer (CEO) and former chief financial officer (CFO) of a company owned by a statutory body on suspicion of abusing their power in the acquisition of shares in two plantation companies worth RM370 million. A source said the two suspects, aged 68 and 60, were arrested at 6.30 pm yesterday when they turned up to give their statements at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya. Meanwhile, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the arrests and said the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Three arrested over alleged smuggling of subsidised cooking oil in Sabah
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Aug 5 — The Sabah Region 4 Marine Police Force (PPM) successfully cracked down on the smuggling of subsidised cooking oil to a neighbouring country in the area along Sungai Siguntur, Sibugal Besar here on Monday. Sabah Region 4 Marine Police Force commander ACP Ahmad Amri Abd Rahman said three individuals were arrested in the 4.30 pm raid along with the seizure of a boat, a three-tonne lorry, and various brands of subsidised cooking oil worth RM160,469. “Sabah Region 4 PPM will continue to intensify intelligence and enforcement operations to combat the leakage and smuggling of subsidised controlled goods,” he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: Queen Raja Zarith Sofiah seeks to create family bonding opportunities for B40 community
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 5 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, yesterday said she plans to organise family programmes for the low-income (B40) community in Johor. The programmes are expected to be held in all districts through the collaboration of the Raja Zarith Sofiah Johor Foundation (YRZSNJ) and the respective district offices, it added. Also present were Johor Bahru district officer Mohd Masni Wakiman and his wife Nurul Asliza Salim; Segamat district officer Mohd Ezzuddin Sanusi and his wife Engku Noorwidainie Engku Aman; the wife of the Mersing district officer, Wan Nor Hanida Wan Ismail; and YRZSNJ chief executive officer Hishamuddin Abdul Rahim.

items.title: Police confirm report on missing Kedah family of three after social media appeal
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 5 — Police yesterday have confirmed receiving a report on the disappearance of a family of three, including a nine-year-old boy, after the case went viral on social media. Kubang Pasu police chief Supt Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the report was lodged on Monday at the Bukit Kayu Hitam Police Station by the woman’s father, who was concerned about the family’s safety after they could not be contacted since July 20. The missing family members are Siti Zulaikha Ahmad Sabri, 36, her husband Khairul Azhar Ahmad, 39, and their son Adid Khairul Azhar, 9.

items.title: Azalina says FOI, Admiralty Bills review to involve wide range of stakeholders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Two Parliamentary Special Select Committees have been given three months to conduct a comprehensive review of the Freedom of Information (FOI) Bill 2026 and the Admiralty Jurisdiction Bill 2026 before submitting recommendations to Parliament. The review reflects the Madani Government’s commitment to advancing legal reforms through a transparent and inclusive parliamentary process, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said the committees would examine various aspects and the scope of the proposed legislation through a series of meetings beginning yesterday.

items.title: Malaysia needs more firms to grow into national champions, regional leaders, says Amir Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Malaysia needs more companies capable of progressing from promising enterprises into national champions and eventually regional leaders, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. He said while companies recognised for their achievements had demonstrated strong performance, the recognition should not mark the end of their ambitions. Companies with market capitalisation between RM100 million and RM1 billion have already distinguished themselves through strong performance.

items.title: Skeletal remains found in Perlis orchard confirmed to be human
items.summary: KANGAR, Aug 5 — Police have confirmed that skeletal remains found inside a gunny sack in an orchard opposite a factory here last month were human. District police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said police were working to establish the identity of the deceased while investigating whether foul play was involved. On July 26, police received a report from a man who discovered the gunny sack while spraying weedkiller in his orchard.

items.title: Tabung Haji reaffirms depositors’ zakat payments valid, Shariah-compliant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has reaffirmed that zakat paid on behalf of its depositors is valid and Shariah-compliant, dismissing doubts over the institution’s zakat payment practices. TH said the National Fatwa Committee for Islamic Religious Affairs Malaysia ruled on May 3, 1979, that while the institution is not required to pay zakat on itself, it is responsible for settling zakat on behalf of its depositors. “TH has consistently fulfilled its obligation to pay zakat on behalf of depositors in accordance with this ruling.

items.title: MACC boosts digital forensics capability to detect AI deepfakes, manipulated evidence
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) continues to strengthen its digital forensic capabilities by participating in the internationally recognised Amped Authenticate course in Trieste, Italy, to better tackle cybercrime and the growing threat of manipulated digital evidence. “This high-impact training covers a range of visual forensic techniques, including metadata analysis, camera fingerprinting, image editing detection, physical consistency assessment, and deepfake detection methods. The MACC said the BFT employs advanced forensic techniques such as Photo Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU) analysis, JPEG Dimples analysis, shadow and reflection analysis, and deepfake detection to scientifically determine whether digital evidence is genuine or has been manipulated.

items.title: 1MDB investigator says he did not check if US$620m returned by Najib was rerouted
items.summary: United Kingdom-based investigator Templeman said this when cross-examined by Najib’s counsel Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah at the trial of 1MDB’s US$5.64 billion civil suit against Najib and six others. Muhammad Shafee: Did you trace whether the US$620 million somehow got rerouted and came back to Najib? Templeman answered “no”.

items.title: MediAsas explained: The RM65 health insurance lifeline coming to Malaysia in 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Malaysians facing the burden of rising medical insurance premiums will soon have a more affordable option. Beginning in 2027, a voluntary medical insurance and takaful plan called MediAsas will be available, with basic monthly premiums starting from RM65. The sustained rise in medical insurance premiums prompted public concern, leading Bank Negara to introduce interim measures in late 2024.

items.title: Industry players: Malaysia’s October ‘mega sports weekend’, led by F1, set to boost sports tourism and economic growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The convergence of several international sporting events in Malaysia this October, including the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix fan activation at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), could provide a major boost to the country’s sports tourism sector and generate wider economic benefits. Inbound tourism expert Uzaidi Udanis described the simultaneous staging of major events, including the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon, Le Tour de Langkawi and the All Stars Legends Football Match from October 2 to 4, as a strategic opportunity to position Malaysia as a regional sports tourism hub. Meanwhile, Tourism Selangor said the F1 Bahrain Grand Prix fan activation would reinforce Malaysia’s standing as a world-class destination for international sporting events.
